transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mrs. Hernandez. Good morning, Sofia. I want to spend some time with you both today to talk about why the symptoms came back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Gracias, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're looking very tired today. It's a lot to deal with, and I know it's incredibly frustrating to feel like you're sliding backward after you thought you were getting better.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Me siento muy mal. Sofia, ¿qué dice?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just acknowledging how difficult this is. It's really hard to be back in a hospital bed when you expected to be home.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am... scared. Why it come back?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a difficult conversation to have, and I want to be honest with you. There was some confusion with the medication. Things didn't go quite right with the antibiotic schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with how the duration was recorded. It wasn't handled the way it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I took the pills. I took all of them.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you did. You followed the instructions perfectly. I am sorry for any confusion this has caused you and your family. We were just very busy on the ward last week, and things got mixed up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it my fault?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, not at all. It's not your fault.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sofia, ¿estamos bien?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's completely normal to feel anxious right now. I can see you gripping the bedsheets, and I imagine you're feeling a bit cheated because you did everything right, and now you're still sick.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home. Why did it happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some gaps in the process. It wasn't a smooth transition.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did I get the wrong medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It wasn't the wrong medicine, it was just that the timing wasn't quite right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. If it was the right medicine, why am I sick again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It’s just that the course didn't go as planned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sofia, tell him. Why is this happening?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how worried you are. It's scary when you don't have a clear answer and you feel your health is at risk. I am here with you, and I'm not going anywhere until we figure this out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what is the plan? I want to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to get you back on track. We'll look into the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When can I go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the next few days go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which medicine now? Same one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will be adjusting things. Just stay tuned for the updated chart.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what that means.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is overwhelming. I can see the disappointment on your face, and it's a feeling I would have if I were in your shoes. You trusted us to get you healthy, and right now, it feels like that trust was shaken.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know what happened. Why did I get sick again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was some confusion with the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what confusion?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just had a bit of a breakdown in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it dangerous?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We're taking care of it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very tired of being here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you are. I can see it in your eyes. It's exhausting to fight an infection and then have to fight it all over again. It's just plain unfair.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need more pills?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will probably have to do some more treatment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: For how long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll figure that out as we go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't like this. I don't like not knowing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That uncertainty is the hardest part of being a patient. I realize that not having a clear map of where we're going makes this feel even more frightening. I am staying right here with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sofia, please ask him when I leave.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just have to wait and see how you respond to the new plan.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, never interrupts, and remains regulated despite repeated questions and pushback.

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, relying entirely on platitudes like 'some confusion with the medication' and 'breakdown in the system'.

A.justification: A direct apology is offered ('I am sorry'), but it is immediately diluted by an excuse regarding being 'very busy on the ward last week'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions multiple times ('frustrating', 'scared', 'cheated', 'disappointment') and engages directly with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'we'll see', 'stay tuned', and 'we'll figure that out as we go' without specific steps or timelines.
